footprint.notes: Microsoft publishes no fifty-state jobs/investment report. The closest is local.microsoft.com's set of state and country 'Microsoft datacenters in …' fact sheets (published October 2025), which give approximate operational datacenter headcount; the state map covers only the seven states whose sheet states a current headcount (AZ, IL, IA, TX, VA, WA, WY). The CA, GA, NC, OH and WI sheets give only a per-building figure ('each datacenter facility employs 50 employees per building') or future hiring, so they are omitted; the India and UK sheets give no headcount; Canada and Denmark give only future headcount; Finland gives a per-building figure; the Greece, Indonesia, Spain, Sweden and Taiwan sheets gave no current headcount in the text extracted. Localized sheets are quoted in their original language. The county-level EY-commissioned datacenter infographics (e.g. Central Washington, Mecklenburg County VA) are sub-state and were not used as state rows. Total employment is only split U.S. vs international in the FY2024 10-K (126,000 / 102,000); the 10-K's long-lived-asset split (U.S. $186,106m vs other countries $115,263m, June 30, 2024) was not recorded as a row because it would duplicate the U.S. country row from a different passage, and it is dominated by goodwill and intangibles. Azure datacenter regions per country were not recorded: Microsoft's geographies pages are current (2026) and do not state a count per country, so any count would be our own tally. No taxes-by-country report was found.

paidout.notes: Fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 (FY2026 Form 10-K, accession 0001193125-26-323660).
